request.contents:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: For the Landlord's records, the Tenant will sign, together with this Agreement, a notice of termination dated for the last day of the term.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
Under the Ontario *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006* (RTA), a tenancy does not automatically end when the fixed term expires; instead, it automatically renews as a month-to-month tenancy unless terminated in accordance with the Act. 

Section 37 of the RTA governs how a tenancy may be terminated by agreement or notice. Specifically, subsection 37(5) expressly prohibits a landlord from requiring or accepting a notice of termination or an agreement to terminate at the time the tenant enters into the tenancy agreement. Any such notice or agreement signed at the beginning of the tenancy is void (save for very narrow exceptions such as certain student housing or care home agreements, which do not apply here).

Because this clause requires the tenant to sign a notice of termination at the same time they enter into the lease agreement, it is void and illegal.

Verdict: not enforceable
Section: 37
